brief: No compatibility with existing operating systems is required, and no hardware or instruction set is emulated; the program format and system interface are the model's own, but scheduling, messages, files and window management must all be run by programs inside the system.

ul: Edit a subsystem's kernel source and restart it, and its behaviour changes; a broken kernel only takes down that subtree.
Execution budget and memory and storage quotas are handed down level by level; kernels, programs, apps and subsystems compete for them, and work is billed by size.
Every level can pause, step, snapshot, restore and fork its child systems; a restore resumes from the saved moment without touching systems outside.

The purple-and-yellow helicopter numbered 24 is kept airborne by a scheduled flight-control process; when budget runs short the control period lengthens and the airframe diverges until it crashes. The default show lasts 15 seconds.

With the network off every level still runs, and only the root browser goes online; ready-made Chromium engines and graphics libraries are allowed, but not a ready-made desktop system or browser interface.

points: **The kernel is a program**: scheduling, messages, files and window management really run as programs inside the system, not as calls back to the host.
**Competition and isolation**: under a shared multi-level budget every process keeps getting time, and a runaway program only hurts its own quota.
**State and causality**: after snapshots, restores and forks, processes, messages, files and images still match the same moment.
**Closed-loop flight**: the flight is decided by the flight-control program, scheduling budget and inputs together, and recordings can be replayed and branched.
scoring: **Mechanisms are 78 points**: the kernel as a program weighs most at 28, closed-loop flight and replay 14, shared resources and isolation 12, and the other three mechanism directions 6–10.
**Interface and apps, 22**: interface design and graphics 17, desktop apps 5.
**Hands-on checks**: graders operate the system themselves, write new programs and edit kernels by the instructions; the work's own tests only assist.
**Logical budget only**: execution budgets and logical time are judged by system behaviour, with no frame rate, throughput or machine-speed tests.
